discovery: Theory of defect-mediated two-dimensional melting and the prediction of the hexatic phase

nominees.name: A. Peter Young
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Santa Cruz, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (statistical mechanics of soft and two-dimensional matter)
motivation: Building on the Kosterlitz-Thouless picture, Halperin and Nelson (1978) and Young (1979) showed that two-dimensional crystals melt in two steps: dislocation unbinding yields a new state of matter, the hexatic phase, with short-range translational but quasi-long-range bond-orientational order, which disclination unbinding then destroys to give an isotropic liquid. The KTHNY theory turned topological defects into the organizing principle of melting and predicted precise, universal signatures, including a renormalized Young's modulus reaching 16π at the transition. Decades of experiments on colloidal monolayers, free-standing liquid-crystal films, electrons on helium and magnetic colloids have confirmed the hexatic phase and its scaling. The idea that bond-orientational order is a distinct broken symmetry now underlies our understanding of liquid crystals, membranes, active matter, and defects on curved surfaces. This work is a textbook example of topology turning geometry into counting, and it predicted a genuinely new phase of matter.
